{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.45,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60", "R59"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.1", "R60.2", "R59.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)", "GND"],
      "observed": "R60 pin 1 sits on Net-(D30-K2), the cathode of the second LED in D30, but R60 pin 2 is on ESTOP_OUT. D30 pin 4 (A2, the anode of that same LED) is also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED and its series resistor therefore both span the same node, so no current can flow and the indicator cannot light. The companion resistor R59 is wired correctly, with pin 2 on GND.",
      "expected": "R60 pin 2 should return to GND, mirroring R59, so that the ESTOP_OUT indicator LED is driven from ESTOP_OUT through R60 to ground.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"67\") (name \"ESTOP_OUT\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") ...) (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")) ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"129\") (name \"Net-(D30-K2)\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") ...) (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"1\") ...))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"128\") (name \"Net-(D30-K1)\") ... (node (ref \"R59\") (pin \"1\") ...) ... and R59 pin 2 listed on GND net 80"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The ESTOP_OUT indicator LED never lights, and R60 is effectively a dead short-circuit loop. The e-stop status indication is lost, though the safety chain itself is unaffected.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D4", "D14", "D23"],
      "pins": ["D4.2", "D14.2", "D23.2"],
      "nets": ["/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW"],
      "observed": "The anodes of the three Ethernet/activity LEDs (D4, D14, D23) are on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, and no other pin on that net drives it. No switch, buffer, regulator or power pin is connected. Its sibling LED-supply net /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV is driven by U34 and has a driver. The Ethernet LEDs therefore have no supply.",
      "expected": "The LED-anode supply net should be driven from a 3.3 V source (a switch, load switch or +3V3), so that the Ethernet and activity LEDs can light.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"32\") (name \"/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D14\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"D23\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"D4\") (pin \"2\") ...))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "Addressable status LEDs (WS2812B, D5-D7, D18-D21) and an analog switch (ISL54222AIUZ, U5) for LED/signal routing."}
      ],
      "impact": "D4, D14 and D23 (Ethernet link/activity and PI activity indicators) cannot be powered, so these status indications are lost.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist and SPICE deck agree, and the main interfaces (CAN, e-stop, USB, Ethernet, I2C sensors, CM4 GPIO) are wired consistently with the spec. Two indicator-LED problems stand out: R60 is connected back to its own ESTOP_OUT node so its LED cannot light, and the anode supply net of three status LEDs has no driver."
}
